review: The hymn is the contemplation of the cross: 1:1–4 is Isa 40:4 with Mark 1:3 and John 9:25, 2:1–8 is Luke 23:34 with Isa 53:5 and Phil 2:8, 3:1–8 is Rev 21:4 with Ps 147:3, and 4:1–8 is 2 Cor 8:9 with John 8:12.
Stanza 1 is four long lines of statement and stanzas 2–4 are eight short lines each, the print's `87.87.87.87 – 12.8.12.8`; the payload keeps the change of gear rather than evening it out.

2:5 עָלָיו הָאַהֲבָה נִגְלָתָה — the Arabic فَوْقَهُ الْحُبُّ تَجَلَّى uses the verb of unveiling; the Hebrew uses the Niphal of גָּלָה, the word of Isa 40:5 (וְנִגְלָה כְּבוֹד יְהוָה), so the cross is where glory is uncovered and not merely where love is felt.
